## TL;DR

Expanded Android Hub fixture QA to 360px and 412px, covering the settings lock control, lock overlay failure and success retries, add-server validation, edit-server sheet, offline fixture, and long content. Review also identified that fixture auth results could be read in production; all fixture query handling is now development-only, with a production-preview regression check for the exact success URL. The development sweep passed 55/55, the production regression passed, the mobile build passed, and `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed.

## Work and rationale

Task #1182 began as a second browser QA pass for Android Hub views missing from #1171. The existing sweep checked the server fixtures at 375px but did not cover the requested 360px and 412px widths. I extended `mobile/scripts/fixture-qa.ts` to visit the existing `many`, `one`, `empty`, `unreachable`, `settings`, `add`, and `discover` fixtures at both widths. It checks element bounds and console errors, exercises the scope control after enabling Device lock, opens the edit sheet with a long server URL, and submits an invalid HTTP URL. The updated first run passed 47 checks.

The first review correctly observed that a settings toggle check does not exercise the locked screen itself. I moved the task back to active through RepoOS before editing the reviewed branch. I added a `lock` browser fixture whose `auth` query result makes browser verification deterministic. The fixture uses the normal reopen-lock flow and renders the actual `LockOverlay`. At both widths, the QA sweep measures the overlay and card, retries with failure and confirms the overlay remains, then changes the fixture result to success and confirms retry closes the overlay. The expanded development sweep passed 55/55.

The second review found a more serious issue: the forced success fixture could be selected in production. I addressed this at fixture selection, not only at the authentication call site. `readHubFixture()` now returns no fixture outside Vite development, so production query parameters cannot select fake server data, force lock settings, or select fixture authentication. `readLockFixtureResult()` also retains a direct development guard as defense in depth. In a production build Vite replaces `import.meta.env.DEV` with `false`.

To exercise the production boundary, I added `mobile/scripts/production-fixture-guard-qa.ts`. It opens the exact `?fixture=lock&auth=success&platform=android` URL against a production Vite preview and verifies the normal empty server state appears without fixture-seeded servers or a lock overlay. This test passed after `bun run build`.

I updated `docs/qa/2026-11-android-hub-second-pass.md` with the methods, observed results, fixture URLs, reproduction command, and boundary between browser overlay checks and native device evidence. No product layout defect was reproduced, so the changes are QA harness coverage and fixture environment hardening rather than CSS changes.

## Approaches tried

The browser automation host was unavailable, so I used the repository's existing Playwright Chromium fixture script against the actual mobile Vite app. A browser shim reported a supported biometric plugin interface, making an unsupported-device warning a poor assertion; the test instead asserts visible settings controls and measured geometry.

For failure and success outcomes, I used a query-controlled dev fixture result and clicked the rendered Retry button. For the production guard, I used a built preview rather than relying only on the dev test, because Vite's production replacement of the DEV constant is part of the security boundary.

## Challenges and blockers

Chromium can validate the Hub overlay's rendered state and retry transitions, but cannot prove Android's native biometric prompt, cancellation behavior, keyboard insets, or physical WebView rendering. The production regression verifies fixture isolation in the production bundle; it is not a real device authentication test. No physical device evidence was collected.

## Key learnings

A settings switch is not coverage for the screen and transitions it enables; review caught the missing lock overlay path. Security-sensitive fixture behavior must be excluded at the fixture-selection boundary as well as at the injected result helper. A production-preview test checks that build-time environment replacement actually prevents the query from choosing fixture state. Browser fixture results and physical device authentication remain separate evidence.
